board.canonical_name: Provable Downstream Consent, Deletion and Purpose Enforcement
Governance and Review of Generative Marketing Content at Volume
Safe, Auditable Agent Execution in Martech Systems
Governed Semantic Context Layer for Agents and Activation
Comparable, Incremental Retail and Commerce Media Measurement
Provenance and Rights Lineage for Generated Creative
Clean Room and Data Collaboration Interoperability
Composable/Warehouse-Native Activation Gap (Latency, State and Copy Sprawl)
AI Intermediation of Owned and Outbound Channels

proposals.name: Measuring and influencing visibility inside AI answer surfaces
proposals.definition: Buyers increasingly complete research inside LLM assistants and AI search results, but there is no reliable way to measure how often a brand is surfaced, cited, or misrepresented there, nor to attribute downstream revenue to that exposure.
proposals.why_unsolved: The blocker is data access plus non-determinism: OpenAI, Google (AI Mode/Overviews), Anthropic, Perplexity and Copilot publish no impression, citation or query-share logs; answers vary by user memory, personalization, model version and routing; many answers produce no referrer at all or collapse into a generic ai.* referral. So-called GEO/AEO tools synthesize a metric by re-prompting a hand-built prompt set through APIs, which is a different distribution from real consumer traffic and cannot be validated against ground truth. There is no equivalent of Search Console, and no incrementality design that works when the exposure itself is unobservable.
proposals.evidence: Organic referral declines reported across publishers and B2B sites through 2025-2026 while branded direct and 'unassigned' traffic grew; a whole vendor category (Profound, Peec, Semrush/Ahrefs AI modules) appeared in 18 months with no agreed metric definitions, which is the signature of an unsolved measurement problem rather than a solved one.

proposals.name: Incrementality inside black-box AI ad buying
proposals.definition: Ad platforms now expose a single AI-optimized objective (Performance Max, Advantage+, agentic buying assistants) while removing placement, query and creative-level reporting, leaving teams unable to determine what the platform actually caused or how to steer it.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platform-reported conversions are modeled and self-attributed; the diagnostic data needed to audit them is deliberately withheld or aggregated. The accepted substitutes both fail at scale: geo/holdout experiments are underpowered for most budgets and channel mixes and take weeks per read, and open-source MMM (Meridian, Robyn) requires experiment calibration that the same teams cannot run, produces wide credible intervals, and yields different answers from different vendors on the same data with no accepted validation standard or benchmark. Platforms also change optimization behavior mid-flight, breaking the stationarity assumptions MMM depends on.
proposals.evidence: Live now because the reporting withdrawal accelerated through 2025-2026 (loss of granular search term and placement detail, forced migration to broad AI campaign types) at the same time MMM was being re-adopted; agencies are openly running 'MMM vs. lift test vs. platform' reconciliation exercises that do not reconcile.

proposals.name: Agentic traffic and agentic checkout break identity, consent and attribution
proposals.definition: When an AI agent browses, compares, and transacts on a user's behalf, marketers cannot tell agent from human, cannot apply consent or personalization correctly, cannot attribute the sale to a touchpoint, and cannot decide whether to serve, block, or price the request.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no widely honored signaling standard for 'this is an agent acting for an identified user with these permissions.' User-agent strings and IP ranges are unreliable and easily spoofed; bot-management systems classify agents as fraud, while agentic commerce protocols (ACP, AP2) standardize payment authorization but not marketing-relevant identity, consent state, or touchpoint provenance. Consent frameworks (TCF, US state opt-outs) assume a human viewing a banner. Analytics tools have no labeled ground-truth set for agent sessions, so even measuring the volume is guesswork, and ad verification cannot certify a human viewed an impression an agent fetched.
proposals.evidence: Agentic checkout moved from demo to production in late 2025 (OpenAI Instant Checkout with Etsy/Shopify, Perplexity buy-with-Pro, Google AP2 with dozens of partners); Cloudflare's default AI-crawler blocking and pay-per-crawl in 2025 forced retailers to make block/allow decisions with no data, and merchants report orders they cannot attribute to any session.

proposals.name: Enforcing consent and deletion downstream of the collection point
proposals.definition: Teams can capture consent and opt-out signals at the edge but cannot prove those signals are honored across the warehouse, activation tools, ad platform audiences, and models already trained on the data.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent is captured as an event, but the stack propagates copies: reverse ETL syncs, uploaded hashed-email audiences at Meta/Google, partner co-op data, agency-held segments, and ML features derived from the person. There is no standard machine-readable purpose/consent token that travels with a record through those hops, and no mechanism to remove an individual's contribution from an already-trained propensity or lookalike model short of retraining. Universal opt-out mechanisms (GPC) are now legally mandatory in several US states but are a browser-level signal with no defined mapping to server-side or CRM-held records. Auditing is manual, so most companies attest rather than verify.
proposals.evidence: Live because the forcing function shifted from Chrome's cookie deprecation (abandoned in 2025) to enforcement: a dozen-plus US state laws in effect with mandatory universal opt-out recognition, Washington/Nevada health-data suits, and a wave of session-replay and pixel wiretapping claims that turn a propagation gap into direct liability.

proposals.name: The review bottleneck on AI-generated marketing content
proposals.definition: Generation capacity vastly exceeds a company's ability to verify that output is factually correct, claim-substantiated, rights-clear, on-brand, and properly disclosed, so throughput is capped by human review rather than by the model.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no reliable automated checker for the things review actually catches: substantiation of a performance claim against approved source material, regulated-industry constraints (MLR, FINRA), licensing scope of a stock or model-trained asset, and consistency with brand meaning rather than brand color values. Brand-governance tools verify surface attributes; they cannot adjudicate semantics or claims. Provenance standards (C2PA) are not carried through ad-serving and social pipelines, so labeling obligations cannot be discharged by metadata alone. EU AI Act transparency duties for synthetic content became applicable in August 2026 with no settled guidance on what constitutes adequate disclosure for marketing creative, which converts a quality problem into a compliance problem.
proposals.evidence: Enterprise pilots repeatedly stall at legal/medical review rather than at generation; agencies report indemnity fights over training-data provenance; the AI Act Article 50 date landing this month makes disclosure operationally urgent with no tooling in market.

proposals.name: Safely letting agents execute inside martech systems
proposals.definition: Teams want agents that actually act — change budgets, send campaigns, edit audiences, update CRM records — but current SaaS permissioning, audit, and rollback models were built for humans and cannot contain an autonomous actor.
proposals.why_unsolved: Martech tools authenticate agents as a human seat or a broad OAuth scope, so there is no per-agent identity, least-privilege scope, or spend/blast-radius cap; audit logs record the borrowed human. MCP connectors proliferated faster than any authorization or provenance model, and prompt injection through the marketing data an agent reads (inbound emails, reviews, web pages, ticket text) remains unmitigated. Most systems of engagement have no transactional rollback for a sent send or a spent budget, so approval gates degrade to a human rubber-stamping every action, which erases the gain.
proposals.evidence: Live because 2025-2026 saw every major suite ship agents (Agentforce, Copilot/Adobe agents, HubSpot Breeze) while security teams blocked write-scope deployments; observed pattern is agents confined to drafting and analysis, which is precisely the symptom of an unresolved control problem.

proposals.name: Cross-network retail and commerce media measurement
proposals.definition: Advertisers spend across hundreds of retail, travel, and financial media networks but cannot compare performance across them, verify reported sales lift, or deduplicate reach and frequency at the shopper level.
proposals.why_unsolved: Each network defines attribution windows, in-store matching, and 'incremental' differently, and reports on its own closed data; log-level access is rare and often contractually withheld. Clean rooms enable a pairwise advertiser-retailer join but not a cross-retailer view, because retailers will not pool identity with competitors and there is no neutral trusted party with sufficient coverage. IAB/MRC standards cover terminology and some measurement guidelines but adoption is voluntary and does not force comparable incrementality methodology, so the standards exist while comparability does not.
proposals.evidence: Live because spend growth continued into 2026 while large CPG advertisers publicly pushed back on non-comparable reporting and began demanding log-level data and independently run holdouts; consolidation of onsite ad tech (Criteo, Topsort, Moloco) has not produced cross-network measurement.

proposals.name: Outbound saturation and the collapse of email/social engagement signals
proposals.definition: AI made outbound volume nearly free and inbox-side AI made engagement unobservable, so lifecycle and B2B teams have neither a working channel economics model nor trustworthy feedback metrics.
proposals.why_unsolved: Open rates were already corrupted by privacy proxies; AI triage, promotional bundling, and assistant-generated summaries now sit between the send and the human, and no mailbox provider exposes whether a message was summarized, deprioritized, or auto-handled. Reputation systems score sending infrastructure, not message quality, so AI-generated near-duplicate outbound degrades whole categories rather than the specific sender; recipients' own AI filters then suppress legitimate mail. On the B2B side, third-party intent data cannot be validated against outcomes, and de-anonymizing site visitors — the usual workaround — became legally risky under state privacy and wiretapping theories.
proposals.evidence: Live because reply and meeting-booked rates fell sharply through 2025-2026 for cold outbound despite Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules taking effect, and vendors pivoted messaging from 'volume' to 'deliverability and warmup', which is an admission the channel's feedback loop is broken.

proposals.name: Measuring AI-mediated discovery
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably quantify how much demand originates in LLM answers, AI Mode, and assistant recommendations, nor what moves that visibility. The channel is now material to revenue but sits outside every deterministic measurement system.
proposals.why_unsolved: There is no supply-side data: no impression counts, no query-level reporting, and often no referrer at all (in-app assistants and agent browsers strip or never send one), so the funnel above the click is unobservable. The substitute — prompt-sampling 'share of model' tools — measures a stochastic system: reported figures show only ~30% of brands stay visible across consecutive runs of the same prompt, so week-over-week deltas are mostly model variance, not marketing effect. No panel or platform-audited truth set exists to calibrate against, so two vendors give a client different numbers and neither can be falsified.
proposals.evidence: Live vendor and practitioner reporting through mid-2026 claims 70%+ of AI referrals are invisible in GA4 and AI contribution is undercounted 3–4x; Perplexity-reported clicks routinely exceed GA4-observed sessions. Guidance published in 2026 still amounts to 'build custom GA4 dimensions and hope,' which is a tell that the primitive is missing, not that teams are lazy.

proposals.name: Agent traffic vs. human traffic in the measurement and personalization layer
proposals.definition: Now that automated agents are a majority of web traffic, teams cannot cleanly separate agent sessions from human sessions, decide which to serve, or interpret metrics that mix the two — so conversion rates, engagement, A/B tests and audience segments are quietly corrupted.
proposals.why_unsolved: Agent identity is unsolved at the point where it matters. Browser-piloting agents (Chrome auto-browse, Comet-class browsers, Claude/OpenAI computer-use) execute inside a real, logged-in user's session with real fingerprints and cookies, so they are indistinguishable from the human by design — signature- and heuristic-based bot detection cannot label them without false-positiving actual customers. Cryptographic attestation (Web Bot Auth-style signed agents) covers only declared server-side crawlers, and adoption is partial and contested. Meanwhile experimentation platforms and analytics tools have no agent dimension to segment on, so the pollution is not even quantified.
proposals.evidence: Cloudflare's CEO stated in June 2026 that bot traffic passed human traffic; HUMAN's 2026 benchmarks put browser-based agents at ~71% of agentic activity with only ~3% touching checkout — i.e. huge top-of-funnel volume that inflates sessions and deflates conversion rate. Cloudflare's September 15, 2026 default block on mixed-use crawlers on ad-bearing pages forces every brand to make a serve/block decision it has no data to make.

proposals.name: Incrementality across fragmented walled gardens and retail media
proposals.definition: Deciding how much of each platform's claimed conversions is incremental, and deduplicating reach across an ever-growing set of closed networks, remains impossible at the granularity and cadence budget decisions require.
proposals.why_unsolved: The blocker is commercial, not statistical: the platforms that would have to supply log-level or deduplicated exposure data are the same parties being audited, and they have no incentive to standardize. Clean rooms permit overlap analysis but not causal counterfactuals, and each network defines 'conversion,' 'impression' and 'attributed sale' differently, so no common denominator exists. Geo-experiments and MMM give trustworthy answers at channel level on a quarterly clock, but media is optimized weekly at tactic/placement level — the resolution gap is structural, and 'triangulation' is a workflow, not a solution.
proposals.evidence: Skai/Stratably's 2026 retail media research finds advertisers on ~6 networks heading to ~11 by end of 2026, with incrementality named the north star yet not actionable; 2026 commentary identifies double-counting across coexisting attribution systems as an architectural failure. Rising retail media and CTV share means the un-measurable slice of the budget is growing, not shrinking.

proposals.name: Getting governed, agent-usable context out of the stack
proposals.definition: AI agents can now call marketing systems, but nobody has a reliable way to give them correct, permissioned, semantically unambiguous context — so agent output is confidently wrong in ways that look plausible.
proposals.why_unsolved: MCP standardized transport and tool discovery, not meaning or entitlements. There is still no shared semantic layer defining what 'active customer,' 'qualified lead' or 'revenue' means across CRM, CDP, warehouse and ad platforms, and no field-level permission or row-level security model that follows an agent across tools — so teams either over-scope agent access (leak and compliance risk) or under-scope it (useless agent). The spec surface is also still moving: the July 2026 stateless MCP revision invalidated architectures built a year earlier, so integration work does not compound.
proposals.evidence: 2026 martech surveys show ~48% of organizations already wiring MCP connectors into assistants while naming context engineering and data integration as the top gap, and data integration has stayed the #1 stack complaint (~66%) even as agent adoption accelerated. The MCP 2026-07-28 stateless spec change is a concrete, dated source of rework.

proposals.name: Enforcing consent and preference downstream, provably
proposals.definition: Capturing consent is solved; proving that a given user's opt-out or Global Privacy Control signal was honored everywhere their data flowed — warehouse, CDP, ad platforms, agents, CTV partners — is not.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent lives as a state at collection time, but activation is a fan-out of copies through reverse-ETL, conversion APIs, offline uploads, clean rooms and now agent-invoked tools, most of which accept data without carrying or re-checking a consent predicate. There is no widely implemented mechanism to attach enforceable policy to the record itself, and no audit artifact that reconstructs 'this signal reached these 14 downstream systems within N hours.' Agentic browsers add a new hole: an agent can accept or ignore a banner on the user's behalf, and no framework says whose consent that is.
proposals.evidence: About a dozen states now mandate honoring GPC, with Indiana, Kentucky and Rhode Island laws effective January 1, 2026 and 2026 amendments in Texas, Oregon, Connecticut and Delaware expanding obligations; state AGs are running sweeps specifically on banner-versus-actual-behavior mismatch. Enforcement has moved from 'do you have a banner' to 'demonstrate the signal was executed,' which is the part the stack cannot produce.

proposals.name: Accountability for decisions made inside black-box automation
proposals.definition: Brands are legally and financially responsible for outcomes produced by platform automation and marketing agents, but cannot audit, evaluate or reproduce the decisions those systems make.
proposals.why_unsolved: The autonomy sits inside vendor systems that expose neither decision logs nor counterfactuals: you cannot see which creative variant, placement or audience an automated campaign chose, cannot hold it fixed to run a clean test, and cannot replay a decision after an incident. There is also no accepted evaluation harness for marketing agents — no benchmark or regression suite that says a bidding or lifecycle agent is safe to widen authority for — so governance defaults to human review gates, which cannot keep pace with the decision rate they are supposed to police.
proposals.evidence: 2026 field guides for agentic media buying converge on 'recommend-only mode' and manual audit trails as the state of the art, and Meta has publicly targeted fully automated ad generation by end of 2026. FTC Section 5 discussion in 2026 makes the beneficiary brand responsible regardless of whether a model made the call, while contracts and platform logs give brands no evidence of reasonable oversight.

proposals.name: Brand and claim governance at generative content velocity
proposals.definition: Content volume has outrun the review, provenance and rights machinery around it, so organizations cannot assert, at scale, that a live asset is on-brand, correctly disclosed, rights-cleared and factually compliant.
proposals.why_unsolved: Compliance and brand conformance are judgments, and there is no trustworthy automated judge — rule-based scanners catch banned words and logo misuse but not misleading implied claims or subtle brand drift, and LLM reviewers are neither consistent nor defensible in an audit. Provenance is worse: C2PA metadata is stripped or invalidated by platform re-encoding and by ordinary editing pipelines, so disclosure obligations cannot be discharged by the asset itself. Rights metadata (talent likeness, licensed music, stock terms) is not carried through generative tools, so derivative assets have no traceable license lineage.
proposals.evidence: Bynder's 2026 DAM research reports roughly three-quarters of content is AI-touched, with governance explicitly lagging; the January 2026 AI transparency/disclosure framework leans on C2PA machine-readable metadata that in practice does not survive distribution. Consumer-side pressure is measurable too — 2026 surveys report large shares of adults reacting negatively to AI content volume in feeds.

proposals.name: Owned channels intermediated by AI recommenders
proposals.definition: Email and other owned channels are now ranked, summarized and deprioritized by AI layers inside the client, and marketers have neither visibility into that ranking nor a trustworthy engagement metric left to optimize against.
proposals.why_unsolved: Authentication and list hygiene — the levers marketers actually control — no longer determine visibility; a message can be authenticated, delivered to the inbox and still be demoted or reduced to a machine-written summary the sender never wrote. Providers publish no diagnostics for this layer, so there is no feedback signal. Compounding it, the metric that engagement-based reputation depends on is corrupted: privacy proxies and AI auto-opens fire opens with no human present, making open rate circular as an input to the very filtering it is meant to explain.
proposals.evidence: Gmail's Gemini-powered inbox rolled out in early 2026 and 2026 deliverability analyses report large shares of inboxed mail being deprioritized rather than spam-foldered, plus auto-opens generated for summarization. This is new in 2026 and distinct from the decade-old 'deliverability is hard' complaint, which was about infrastructure a team could fix.

proposals.name: Privacy-resilient causal measurement
proposals.definition: Marketers still cannot reliably determine the incremental effect of campaigns across walled gardens, retail media, CTV, mobile, search and offline sales. Attribution, media-mix modeling and experiments routinely produce incompatible answers at the budget and audience granularity where decisions are made.
proposals.why_unsolved: The required counterfactual is usually unobservable; platforms restrict user-level data and grade their own performance; identity loss breaks paths; and controlled experiments are expensive, contaminated by overlapping media and difficult to run continuously. No current method simultaneously provides causal validity, cross-channel coverage, speed and granular optimization.
proposals.evidence: Signal loss has moved from a browser-cookie issue to a broader fragmentation problem spanning platform privacy controls, mobile identifiers, clean rooms and proliferating retail-media networks. The continuing investment in incrementality platforms, geo-testing and next-generation MMM—without convergence on a trusted result—shows that this remains active.

proposals.name: Consent-aware identity and reach management
proposals.definition: There is no dependable way to recognize, suppress, frequency-cap or personalize for the same consenting person across browsers, apps, CTV, commerce media, CRM and offline interactions. This creates both wasted reach and privacy risk.
proposals.why_unsolved: No identifier is simultaneously ubiquitous, accurate, durable and acceptable under differing laws and platform policies. Deterministic IDs have limited coverage, probabilistic matching has uncertain error rates, and clean rooms can compare only the identities and data their participants already possess.
proposals.evidence: Media consumption and activation continue shifting into authenticated but mutually isolated ecosystems, especially CTV and retail media. The coexistence of multiple identity frameworks rather than consolidation around one interoperable standard is evidence that the problem remains unresolved.

proposals.name: End-to-end privacy-rights and data-lineage enforcement
proposals.definition: Organizations cannot reliably propagate consent changes, deletion requests, purpose restrictions and retention rules through every warehouse table, SaaS export, audience, clean room, model feature and generated artifact containing or derived from a person's data.
proposals.why_unsolved: Most stacks lack field-level lineage across organizational and vendor boundaries, while copied and derived data lose their connection to the original consent record. Vendors expose inconsistent deletion controls, laws differ by jurisdiction and it remains technically ambiguous when a trained model or aggregate is sufficiently detached from personal data.
proposals.evidence: The rapid expansion of first-party data activation, clean rooms and generative-AI workflows is creating more derivatives and destinations just as privacy obligations are becoming more granular. Consent-management products can record choices, but they still cannot prove enforcement throughout the downstream stack.

proposals.name: Interoperable data collaboration and clean rooms
proposals.definition: Brands, publishers and media platforms cannot easily perform comparable audience, overlap and measurement analyses across multiple clean rooms. Results often depend on the host platform, matching method and permitted query rather than a shared analytical truth.
proposals.why_unsolved: Clean rooms do not create missing identity coverage or neutralize incentives. They use incompatible schemas, identity namespaces, privacy thresholds, query languages and governance rules, while dominant platforms limit export and independent validation.
proposals.evidence: Clean-room adoption has produced a growing collection of platform-specific environments rather than a common collaboration layer. Teams increasingly need several rooms and substantial custom engineering to answer what appears to be the same business question.

proposals.name: Reliable governance of generative marketing content
proposals.definition: Teams cannot safely automate high-volume generation of copy, images, video and customer interactions while guaranteeing factual accuracy, brand compliance, legal clearance, provenance and consistent behavior across markets.
proposals.why_unsolved: Models are probabilistic and can fail on rare but consequential cases; automated evaluators share blind spots with generators; rights and provenance metadata are incomplete; and human review removes much of the promised speed at large scale. Retrieval and guardrails reduce errors but do not provide enforceable guarantees.
proposals.evidence: Content generation has moved from isolated experimentation into production workflows and customer-facing agents, making low-frequency failures materially consequential. The market's emphasis on guardrails, evaluation, approval layers and provenance—rather than dependable unattended deployment—indicates unresolved operational risk.

proposals.name: A trustworthy customer-data semantic and activation layer
proposals.definition: Even well-funded companies struggle to maintain one operational meaning for customers, events, audiences, product attributes and metrics across warehouses, CDPs, analytics tools and execution platforms. Audiences that look identical on paper frequently differ in membership, freshness and eligibility.
proposals.why_unsolved: Source events and business definitions change continuously, identity resolution is uncertain, and each destination transforms or delays data differently. Warehouse-native architectures reduce copying but do not resolve semantics, source quality, ownership or reconciliation between analytical and operational state.
proposals.evidence: The shift from packaged CDPs toward composable and warehouse-native stacks has exposed that storage consolidation is not semantic consolidation. AI agents increase the urgency because automated decisions amplify ambiguous definitions and undocumented data quality failures.

proposals.name: Cross-channel journey orchestration with global control
proposals.definition: Marketing systems still cannot optimize a customer's overall experience across email, messaging, web, apps, advertising, commerce and service channels. Most optimize the next action inside one channel while creating contradictory offers, excessive contact or locally optimal but globally harmful outcomes.
proposals.why_unsolved: Channel platforms expose uneven APIs and delayed feedback, customer state is incomplete, and there is no agreed objective function balancing conversion, margin, fatigue, service outcomes and long-term value. Organizational ownership and independent channel budgets further prevent a single decision layer from controlling execution.
proposals.evidence: The rise of real-time decisioning and agentic orchestration has increased expectations, but production implementations still rely heavily on rules, channel-specific models and manually negotiated suppression policies. Vendors advertise autonomous journeys more readily than they demonstrate independent, sustained lift across channels.

proposals.name: Visibility and measurement inside AI answer interfaces
proposals.definition: Marketers lack dependable methods to understand or influence how brands and products appear in generative search, assistants and other answer interfaces, especially when an answer produces awareness or conversion without a conventional click.
proposals.why_unsolved: Answer generation is opaque, dynamic and often personalized; citations are inconsistent; prompt-level impression data is unavailable; referral signals are incomplete; and there is no stable equivalent to rankings, share of voice or attribution. Synthetic prompt panels cannot establish what real users saw or whether exposure caused an outcome.
proposals.evidence: Discovery is moving from lists of links toward synthesized answers while analytics remain centered on pages, clicks and referrals. The emergence of answer-engine visibility tools based largely on repeated synthetic queries demonstrates demand, but their inability to observe actual population-level exposure shows the central measurement gap.

proposals.name: Decision-grade cross-channel causal measurement
proposals.definition: Marketers still cannot reliably determine the incremental business impact of spend across walled gardens, CTV, retail media, creators, gaming, search and offline channels. Attribution, experiments and marketing-mix models frequently produce conflicting answers.
proposals.why_unsolved: Platforms restrict exposure and outcome data; channels use incompatible definitions; identity signals are incomplete; experiments cannot cover every interaction; and MMM still underrepresents newer channels. AI can accelerate modeling but cannot recover inaccessible data or resolve contradictory incentives and standards.
proposals.evidence: IAB’s February 2026 State of Data report says measurement is at a “breaking point,” citing signal loss, inconsistent channel representation and unreliable exposure-to-outcome links. IAB subsequently launched Project Eidos to address the underlying fragmentation rather than offer another point solution. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/IAB_StateofDataReport_February_2026pdf.pdf?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Safe, auditable autonomy for marketing agents
proposals.definition: Teams cannot yet let agents independently change budgets, launch creative, contact customers or optimize journeys while reliably keeping every action accurate, authorized, compliant and on-brand.
proposals.why_unsolved: Agent behavior is probabilistic, errors can compound across workflows, and conventional approval and access-control systems were designed for deterministic software and human operators. Production systems still lack mature action-level permissions, evaluation, rollback, incident response and end-to-end audit trails.
proposals.evidence: Only 8% of CMOs surveyed by BCG run campaigns with multiple autonomous agents, while Salesforce respondents cited security, data integrity, legal compliance, brand consistency and limited visibility into AI actions as major concerns. A separate 2026 survey found only one in five organizations had practiced an AI-failure response plan. ([bcg.com](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2026/making-the-agentic-marketing-transformation-a-reality?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Measuring influence inside AI-mediated discovery
proposals.definition: Brands cannot reliably measure whether—and why—ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews and other answer systems mention, recommend or misrepresent them, nor connect that influence to later purchases.
proposals.why_unsolved: Answers are probabilistic and personalized; prompt populations are unknowable; model and retrieval changes alter results without notice; platforms expose little impression or journey data; and much of the resulting demand later appears as direct traffic, branded search or another channel.
proposals.evidence: IAB reported in August 2026 that more than 20 AI-visibility vendors use incompatible methods and can return different answers for the same brand. WFA found that only 6% of participating global brands had clear ownership, strategy and measurement for AI visibility, despite 96% expecting major impact. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/guidelines/measuring-visibility-in-the-ai-era/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: An agent-ready customer and brand context layer
proposals.definition: Even well-funded teams cannot consistently give personalization and AI systems a current, permissioned and semantically coherent view of the customer, product catalogue, brand rules and business state across marketing, sales, service and commerce.
proposals.why_unsolved: The same customer, product and metric are represented differently across systems; identity resolution remains probabilistic; unstructured knowledge lacks dependable metadata; and lineage, freshness and access policies are lost when context is assembled dynamically. A CDP or data warehouse alone does not supply the business meaning agents need.
proposals.evidence: Salesforce found marketers had complete access to service, sales and commerce data only 58%, 56% and 51% of the time, respectively. Deloitte reported that data searchability and reusability remain major barriers to agentic automation, while BCG identified data foundations and brand-intelligence layers as differentiators that most organizations have not built. ([salesforce.com](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/state-of-marketing-2026/?bc=OTH&ver=1778596287&utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: End-to-end consent and privacy-policy enforcement
proposals.definition: Organizations cannot reliably ensure that a consumer’s consent, opt-out, deletion request and permitted purposes propagate correctly through every tag, identity graph, activation platform, model, clean room and downstream partner.
proposals.why_unsolved: Consent-management systems commonly govern collection but not every later use; identifiers and records diverge across systems; downstream vendors interpret signals differently; and the expanding patchwork of state and international rules changes which purposes and data classes are allowed. Current tooling often records a preference without proving enforcement.
proposals.evidence: IAB introduced a revised multi-state agreement effective June 2, 2026 because advertisers remained unprepared for increasing state-law complexity. IAPP documented additional state requirements coming online in 2026, while IAB Tech Lab continues to update privacy-signaling and deletion frameworks—evidence that interoperable enforcement is still being built. ([iab.com](https://www.iab.com/blog/advertiser-privacy-compliance-solution-arrives/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Comparable, incremental retail and commerce-media measurement
proposals.definition: Advertisers still cannot compare retail-media networks on an apples-to-apples basis or distinguish genuine incremental sales from purchases that would have occurred anyway.
proposals.why_unsolved: Each retailer controls its own purchase data, attribution windows, identity matching, ad formats and reporting logic. Closed-loop reports therefore over-credit platforms, while deduplication across retailers, open-web media, stores and marketplaces remains incomplete.
proposals.evidence: In 2026, IAB Europe said buyers and sellers still lack a common measurement language, and IAB identified inconsistent definitions, measurement and operating frameworks as barriers to scaling commerce media. ANA likewise says RMNs provide limited performance visibility and remain difficult to compare. ([iabeurope.eu](https://iabeurope.eu/measurement-that-the-market-can-trust-reflections-from-the-iab-europe-retailer-leaders-council/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Interoperability among agents, martech platforms and data clean rooms
proposals.definition: A marketing workflow cannot yet move safely across independently developed agents, clouds, clean rooms, ad platforms and systems of record while preserving identity, context, permissions, state and accountability.
proposals.why_unsolved: APIs connect applications but do not provide a shared model for delegated authority, agent identity, semantic context, privacy signals, transaction state or failure handling. Emerging protocols compete or cover only slices of the problem, while major platforms retain proprietary data and execution environments.
proposals.evidence: IAB Tech Lab was still developing and updating agentic-advertising protocols in 2026 to establish agent identity, verification, privacy signaling and common taxonomies. McKinsey similarly described MCP, A2A and transaction protocols as additions still needed for governed agent integration. ([iabtechlab.com](https://iabtechlab.com/standards/aamp-agentic-advertising-management-protocols/?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Verifiable provenance and rights for generated creative
proposals.definition: Marketing organizations cannot reliably prove how every generated or modified asset was made, which source material and likeness rights it used, whether disclosure is required, and whether provenance survives distribution.
proposals.why_unsolved: Generation tools retain inconsistent lineage; platform labels and legal requirements differ; asset metadata can be stripped or lost through editing and syndication; and provenance standards attest to recorded history rather than proving that training data, claims or likeness use were authorized.
proposals.evidence: WFA found 78% of global brands were already using AI-generated or enhanced consumer content, but 61% struggled with fragmented regulatory obligations and 80% wanted global guidance. IAB issued its first disclosure framework in January 2026, and C2PA was still publishing implementation guidance in July—showing that production adoption has outrun dependable provenance infrastructure. ([wfanet.org](https://wfanet.org/knowledge/item/2026/04/02/global-brands-call-for-clearer-consensus-on-ai-labelling-as-usage-accelerates-wfa-research?utm_source=openai))

proposals.name: Cross-Platform Incrementality Disconnect Across Walled Gardens
proposals.definition: The mathematical and structural inability to compute unified, cross-network incremental lift across walled gardens that each enforce non-interoperable privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) and aggregated clean rooms.
proposals.why_unsolved: Ad platforms (Google, Meta, Amazon, TikTok) restrict raw user-level log exports and mandate disparate aggregation thresholds, differential privacy noise additions, and incompatible clean room query schemas that mathematically prevent global causal deduplication.
proposals.evidence: Marketing teams using modern data clean rooms still have to rely on fragmented media-mix models (MMM) because deterministic cross-network multi-touch attribution cannot reconcile conflicting differential privacy noise budgets across networks.

proposals.name: Attribution and Intent Distortion from Agentic AI Traffic
proposals.definition: The inability of web tracking, analytics, and personalization engines to distinguish human exploratory behavior from automated LLM agents, web crawlers, and AI-driven personal assistants acting on behalf of users.
proposals.why_unsolved: AI agents execute dynamic JavaScript, emulate residential IP pools, and generate realistic session interactions without user-agent flags, breaking behavioral scoring, conversion funnels, and real-time site personalization triggers.
proposals.evidence: Analytics platforms exhibit massive surges in deep-session engagement with zero downstream conversion, forcing engineering teams to build custom heuristic filters that routinely over-block genuine high-intent human traffic.

proposals.name: First-Party Identity Graph Decay from Ephemeral Browser Storage
proposals.definition: The rapid fragmentation and decay of first-party cookie/ID graphs caused by aggressive platform-level client-side storage capping (e.g., Apple ITP, Safari 7-day limits, and Android Privacy Sandbox constraints).
proposals.why_unsolved: Server-side tagging and CNAME cloaking are increasingly detected and throttled by browser heuristics and ISP-level protections, leaving no compliant mechanism to link anonymous multi-session customer journeys that exceed 7 to 14 days without persistent authenticated logins.
proposals.evidence: Brands with consideration cycles longer than two weeks report first-party CRM match rates degrading rapidly, requiring continuous re-identification and artificially skewing new-vs-returning visitor ratios.

proposals.name: Deterministic Semantic Compliance for Real-Time GenAI Personalization
proposals.definition: The absence of zero-latency, deterministic guardrails that prevent real-time generative marketing engines from hallucinating non-compliant pricing, terms, or brand-inconsistent messaging during dynamic 1:1 customer interactions.
proposals.why_unsolved: Probabilistic large multimodal models cannot guarantee 100% adherence to complex, fast-changing legal/regulatory matrices (e.g., FTC disclosure rules, regional pricing constraints) within standard 50ms real-time ad serving or dynamic web delivery latency budgets.
proposals.evidence: Enterprises restrict generative AI tooling to offline asset pre-generation and internal approval workflows rather than executing live runtime generative copy assembly at the point of delivery.

proposals.name: Composable CDP Latency and State Consistency Gaps
proposals.definition: The failure of warehouse-native/composable customer data platforms (CDPs) to achieve sub-second, bi-directional state synchronization between cloud data warehouses and edge customer touchpoints.
proposals.why_unsolved: Columnar cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery) are engineered for high-throughput batch and micro-batch analytical processing rather than ultra-low-latency, point-lookup ACID transactions required by real-time mobile app triggers and POS systems.
proposals.evidence: Engineering teams frequently operate dual data architectures—a composable warehouse pipeline alongside a legacy real-time transactional event hub—re-introducing the exact data fragmentation composable architectures were purchased to eliminate.

proposals.name: Multi-Agent Automation Orchestration and Collision Governance
proposals.definition: The lack of orchestration frameworks to manage competing autonomous optimization algorithms operating simultaneously across different stages of the martech stack.
proposals.why_unsolved: Optimization engines (e.g., automated bidding in ad platforms, dynamic on-site pricing algorithms, automated CRM journey triggers) operate in closed feedback loops without standardized inter-agent communication protocols, resulting in race conditions and cannibalization.
proposals.evidence: Simultaneous execution of automated discounting engines and algorithm-driven retention journeys causes automated price erosion and unpredictable customer messaging conflicts that must be manually overridden.

proposals.name: Asset Provenance and Digital Rights Sprawl in Automated Creative Systems
proposals.definition: The inability to reliably track licensing rights, localized consent, training provenance, and derivative ownership across millions of modular, dynamically generated creative variations.
proposals.why_unsolved: Digital asset management (DAM) systems lack native cryptographic provenance pipelines and real-time metadata lineage tracking capable of binding source asset licenses (e.g., talent likeness, regional stock rights) to dynamically composited downstream synthetic assets.
proposals.evidence: Legal and brand ops bottlenecks in generative creative production have shifted from asset creation speed to post-generation rights auditing, stalling the deployment of scaled creative automation.

proposals.name: Consent State Propagation Across Distributed Asynchronous Pipelines
proposals.definition: The failure to reliably enforce and audit real-time consumer consent revocations (such as Global Privacy Control or opt-out requests) across decoupled, downstream asynchronous data pipelines and microservices.
proposals.why_unsolved: Event-driven, distributed data architectures decouple ingestion from consumption, resulting in eventual consistency where a consent revocation takes hours to propagate across edge caches, third-party webhook sinks, and mirrored analytics partitions.
proposals.evidence: Global privacy audits consistently surface edge cases where user data was processed for targeted activation hours or days after explicit opt-out was logged at the consent management platform (CMP) layer.

proposals.name: Triangulated Measurement Reconciliation
proposals.definition: Marketing organizations cannot systematically reconcile conflicting performance signals produced by media mix modeling (MMM), randomized incrementality testing, and deterministic/probabilistic attribution models into a single operational decision engine.
proposals.why_unsolved: The underlying methodologies operate on mathematically incompatible assumptions, data granularities, and time horizons. Top-down MMM relies on aggregated historical elasticity with latency, randomized holdout testing is episodic and expensive to run continuously, and bottom-up attribution is structurally impaired by browser/OS privacy restrictions and walled-garden opacity.
proposals.evidence: In 2026 industry benchmarks, over 75% of marketing leaders report making budget allocation decisions using incomplete data, and fewer than a quarter successfully operationalize MMM for live campaign optimization due to continuous variance with incrementality tests.

proposals.name: Warehouse-Native Activation Boundary Leakage
proposals.definition: The architectural promise of composable martech—centralizing customer data within the cloud data warehouse without copying PII—fails during reverse-ETL activation across downstream execution tools.
proposals.why_unsolved: Downstream activation platforms (ESPs, ad networks, SMS gateways) require local data caching, specialized schema transformations, and state persistence to execute low-latency delivery, forcing reverse-ETL pipelines to duplicate and fragment customer PII across vendor boundaries and creating compliance drift.
proposals.evidence: The aggressive push by cloud lakehouses (such as Databricks' native CustomerLake and Snowflake-native marketing apps) in 2026 reflects practitioner dissatisfaction with brittle reverse-ETL sync caches and multi-vendor PII duplication.

proposals.name: Zero-Click AI Search (GEO/AEO) Visibility and Attribution
proposals.definition: Marketers cannot track, measure, or attribute upstream brand discovery and conversions originating from conversational AI engines, LLM answer summaries, and autonomous shopping agents.
proposals.why_unsolved: Conversational AI platforms act as zero-click intermediaries that ingest unstructured web content without passing traditional HTTP referrers, UTM parameters, or impression logs back to brand domains, rendering traditional clickstream analytics completely blind.
proposals.evidence: With over 50% of consumers utilizing generative AI for search and shopping discovery in 2026, search marketing teams are experiencing unexplained surges in unclassified direct traffic and baseline organic attribution collapse.

proposals.name: Protocol-Level Identity Graph Decay
proposals.definition: Enterprise identity resolution systems cannot reliably maintain persistent cross-device, cross-channel customer identities across owned properties, retail media networks, and walled gardens.
proposals.why_unsolved: Operating system sandboxing, browser-level IP masking, private relay networks, and stringent data-sharing laws have systematically stripped deterministic linkable signals, while probabilistic matching algorithms suffer compounding error rates across multi-device user journeys.
proposals.evidence: First-party identity graphs in 2026 show unprecedented identity fragmentation rates, with customer records decaying faster than reverse-ETL or CDP graph algorithms can reconcile without authenticated logins.

proposals.name: Synthetic Asset Governance at Scale
proposals.definition: Marketing teams lack automated, programmatic guardrails to enforce brand identity, copyright compliance, claim accuracy, and regional regulatory constraints across high-velocity generative-AI content pipelines.
proposals.why_unsolved: Generative AI foundational models lack deterministic compliance enforcement mechanisms at runtime, while traditional digital asset management (DAM) and review systems rely on manual review queues that cannot scale with dynamically generated variations.
proposals.evidence: Chiefmartec and industry survey data in 2026 show that while content AI tools saw massive initial adoption, only 8% of enterprise organizations report confidence in their automated AI governance frameworks, driving a market shakeout among un-governed AI point solutions.

proposals.name: Semantic Context Engineering for Agentic Martech
proposals.definition: Autonomous marketing AI agents fail to execute complex multi-step campaign operations because enterprise data lacks a standardized semantic layer that encodes real-world business context and operational rules.
proposals.why_unsolved: Enterprise marketing logic (such as cohort suppression rules, brand constraints, and seasonal margin thresholds) resides in tacit human knowledge and unstructured documentation rather than unified, queryable ontologies that AI agents can parse without hallucinating.
proposals.evidence: Despite ubiquitous marketing vendor announcements of autonomous 'agentic' workflows in 2025 and 2026, real-world enterprise deployments remain confined to narrowly scoped, human-in-the-loop deterministic automations.

proposals.name: The Marketing-Data Engineering Operational Stalemate
proposals.definition: The structural friction between central IT/data teams prioritizing governance and marketing ops teams requiring rapid, self-serve data schema adaptations prevents timely campaign execution.
proposals.why_unsolved: Central data teams manage data pipelines via strict CI/CD, schema stability, and cost-control protocols, whereas marketing operations require rapid experimentation, unstructured event capture, and real-time activation, creating persistent operational backlogs.
proposals.evidence: Recent enterprise martech surveys show 78% of marketing leaders report their tech stack falls short of driving core business objectives, with the 'activation gap' between IT-managed lakehouses and marketing end-users cited as the leading organizational barrier.

proposals.name: Sub-Second Omnichannel State Orchestration
proposals.definition: Inability to dynamically determine and deliver the next-best-action across web, mobile, in-store, and customer service touchpoints within millisecond latency budgets.
proposals.why_unsolved: Architectural tension persists between the depth of the customer profile (stored in analytical data warehouses) and the speed of execution engines (which require sub-100ms response times at the edge), forcing teams to choose between rich contextual intelligence and real-time responsiveness.
proposals.evidence: Leading retail and financial services brands in 2026 continue to report high fail rates when attempting to merge batch-computed propensity scores with edge-based event triggers during active user sessions.
